newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower, Novartis eases on debut.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower, Novartis eases on debut.

text.p: Swiss shares closed lower in thin volumes as Novartis, the newly created world number two in pharmaceuticals, ended its first day of trading below opening levels.
After trading closed, CS Holding announced it was selling its stake in the industrial activities of Elektrowatt to German group Siemens AG, resulting in over two billion Swiss francs in revenue.

Shares in Novartis ended near the day's low, with registered shares at 1,488 and bearers at 1,485 after both opened at 1,502 Swiss francs on the first day of trading since the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz on Friday.
"People may have expected more on the first day of trading", one trader said.
Novartis made its debut after Ciba and Sandoz last week received final U.S. approval to merge. Sandoz registereds closed on Friday at 1,494 Sfr and Ciba registereds ended at 1,595 Sfr.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was down 14.6 points, or 0.38 percent, to 3,875.5.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended off 6.46 points, or 0.26 percent, at 2,475.22 points.
Dealers said investors were virtually absent and activity largely was reduced to professional trade and some position squaring. Some shares were depressed by profit taking.
Roche certificates ended 50 francs down at 10,190. On the other hand, chemical firm added four francs to 577, reaching a new closing high.
Electrowatt slumped 2.7 percent to 511 francs, suffering from a large sell order from abroad. One dealer said the stock could also be pressured by a UBS downgrade.
Among the winners were Holderbank, ABB, Swissair, Surveillance and Zurich insurance. Swissair soared 1.7 percent to 1,070 francs due to a technical reaction to last week's losses, a dealer said.
UBS sank 22 francs to 1,174. The weakness may partially stem from switches to other financials.
CS Holding gained 0.50 francs to 137.50. Insurer Zurich also firmed, advancing two francs to 366. SBC was flat at 250.50 francs.
CS Holding said it was selling its 44.9 percent stake in the industrial business of Elektrowatt after selling most of its same-size holding in Elektrowatt's utility division on Friday.
